newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian rights activist says Israel bans travel.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian rights activist says Israel bans travel.

text.p: A leading Palestinian human rights activist said on Monday Israel had banned him from travelling to Norway for a conference on "Citizenship and the State in the Middle East".

Iyad al-Sarraj, director of the Palestinian Commission for Citizen's Rights and the Gaza Mental Health Programme, said he was told by Israeli authorities he could not leave PLO-ruled Gaza for security reasons.
Under Israeli-PLO peace deals, Israel maintains overall control of borders in Gaza and the West Bank.
"This is unjustified and unacceptable. I have no security violations and what happened shows how Israel still controls the movement of Palestinians even after peace," Sarraj told Reuters.
A spokesman for the coordinator of Israeli affairs in Palestinian areas said he was checking the report.

Sarraj, an outspoken critic of the peace deals, was jailed twice this year by the Palestinian Authority in Gaza on defamation charges -- later dropped -- after he attacked its human rights record in a New York Times interview.

He said he believed he was banned from travelling to Monday's conference in Oslo because of a strongly worded statement he issued on Sunday criticising an Israeli High Court decision on Israeli interrogation methods.
The High Court overturned an interim court order barring the Israeli Security Services from using force to extract information from a suspected militant of the Islamic Jihad movement.
